sourceReviews.supportingSummary: Fresh v4 inspection of the entire ConfigMap unit confirms process environment initialization at Pod start, the explicit environment/subPath automatic-update exclusions, and ordinary volume projection updates. The scenario separately guarantees C observed current file and per-request reread, so no application autoreload or instantaneous projection is inferred. The new C-Pod preservation restriction is actually authored, not inferred from availability. a: The freshly reread ConfigMap unit excludes subPath from automatic refresh and initializes new Pod configuration from the source. The alternate context changes prior freshness, not B consumption mode. b: The source initializes environment values when Pods start and says existing ConfigMap environment variables do not automatically update. The alternate case preserves that exact contract. c: The source separates environment and subPath nonrefreshing consumers from ordinary updating volumes. The stem independently supplies C current file, application reread and an explicit no-restart/no-replacement rule. d: New Pods initialize configuration from the ConfigMap. No source claim that all rolling updates cause downtime is needed: the actual v4 prohibition is replacement of existing C Pods themselves.

choiceReviews.rationale: Refreshing only A leaves B current pre-update Pods with their old subPath projection, so not all three applications receive the updated configuration. Alternate context: B still uses subPath but its existing Pods are already post-update replacements with current configuration, C is already current, and only A remains stale. Evidence: The freshly reread ConfigMap unit excludes subPath from automatic refresh and initializes new Pod configuration from the source. The alternate context changes prior freshness, not B consumption mode.

Refreshing only B leaves A current pre-update Pods consuming the old process-start environment, which cannot receive this update by waiting. Alternate context: A retains environment-at-startup consumption but its existing Pods already obtained current values through an earlier post-update replacement, so only B now needs new Pods and C is current. Evidence: The source initializes environment values when Pods start and says existing ConfigMap environment variables do not automatically update. The alternate case preserves that exact contract.

This key is not incorrect: A and B both need fresh Pod initialization, while C already has the updated ordinary-volume file and rereads it without replacing any existing C Pod. Alternate context: A/B Pods predate the update, their environment/subPath modes are unchanged, and every protected C Pod continues reading its already refreshed ordinary projected file as specified. Evidence: The source separates environment and subPath nonrefreshing consumers from ordinary updating volumes. The stem independently supplies C current file, application reread and an explicit no-restart/no-replacement rule.

A full new-Pod rollout could refresh configuration but replaces C existing Pods, directly violating the written restriction regardless of application availability. Alternate context: Replacement is allowed for all three Deployments and all are intentionally reinitialized from current configuration, for example when every application reads configuration only on startup. Evidence: New Pods initialize configuration from the ConfigMap. No source claim that all rolling updates cause downtime is needed: the actual v4 prohibition is replacement of existing C Pods themselves.

reviews.verificationNotes: Fresh v4 adversarial review challenged every literal action against the complete current ConfigMap evidence. A-only and B-only are valid when the other nonrefreshing consumer already has current replacement Pods, but not under the supplied pre-update state. Full rollout is valid elsewhere but violates the explicit preservation of every existing C Pod, even if it preserves service availability. Selective A+B is uniquely supported. This new-hash verdict does not change the v1/v3 holds or any v2 result, and no earlier rubric or approval was inherited.
reviews.confidenceReason: The actual source establishes distinct consumption refresh rules, while the exact v4 text supplies both freshness state and a Pod-identity restriction. All four literal actions now have grounded contexts without impossible waiting or downtime assumptions.
